questions.prompt: Tell me about your favorite teacher.
questions.sampleA1: I like my teacher. She is nice. She helps me. She is good.
questions.sampleA2: I like my teacher, Mr. Lee. He is funny and he teaches math. I like math because it is interesting. He is very kind to me.
questions.sampleB1: My favorite teacher was my history teacher. I think he was very good because he made history interesting. He told a lot of stories, and the stories helped me remember the dates. Also, he was always willing to help students after class. I learned a lot from him.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, my favourite teacher has to be my English teacher from secondary school, Mr. Karimov. He had this amazing knack for making even the dullest topics come alive. What really stood out was how patient he was — he never made you feel silly for asking questions. I suppose he's a big part of why I fell in love with languages in the first place.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menga o'qituvchim yoqadi. U yaxshi. U menga yordam beradi. U a'lochi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menga o'qituvchim, janob Li yoqadi. U hazilkash va matematika o'rgatadi. Menga matematika yoqadi, chunki u qiziqarli. U menga juda mehribon.
questions.uzSampleB1: Mening eng sevimli o'qituvchim tarix o'qituvchim edi. Menimcha, u juda yaxshi edi, chunki u tarixni qiziqarli qilib qo'ydi. U ko'p hikoyalar aytib berardi va hikoyalar menga sanalarni eslab qolishga yordam berardi. Bundan tashqari, u har doim darsdan keyin o'quvchilarga yordam berishga tayyor edi. Men undan juda ko'p narsa o'rgandim.
questions.uzSampleB2: Mening eng sevimli o'qituvchim, ehtimol, maktabning oxirgi yilidagi fizika o'qituvchim edi. U murakkab tushunchalarni tushunarli qilish qobiliyatiga ega edi, bu fizika sohasida oson ish emas! U bizni tanqidiy fikrlashga va hamma narsaga shubha bilan qarashga undadi, bu menga juda yoqdi. Uni ajratib turadigan narsa, uning fanga bo'lgan chinakam ishtiyoqi edi, uni u juda samarali tarzda yetkazardi. U bizga faqat formulalarni o'rgatmay, balki atrofimizdagi dunyoni chuqurroq tushunishga yordam berardi. Uning tufayli men universitetda fizika o'qishni o'ylab qoldim.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Tell me about your favorite teacher.
idioms: take someone under one's wing - "birovni himoya qilmoq"
sentenceStarters: "My favorite teacher was..." - "Mening sevimli o'qituvchim ... edi..."
"What made them special was..." - "Ularni alohida qilgan narsa ... edi..."
"They had a profound impact on me because..." - "Ular menga katta ta'sir ko'rsatdi, chunki..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
My favorite teacher was my high school English teacher, Mrs. Johnson. She had a profound impact on my education and genuinely inspired my love for languages.
What made her special was her teaching style. She didn't just lecture – she made lessons interactive and engaging. She would use games, debates, and real-world examples to make the subject come alive. Her enthusiasm for the subject was contagious.
Beyond academics, she was incredibly supportive. She took time to understand each student's strengths and weaknesses and always encouraged us to push beyond our limits. She believed in me even when I doubted myself. As they say, "A good teacher can inspire hope, ignite imagination, and instill a love of learning." She certainly did all of that for me.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Mening eng sevimli o'qituvchim o'rta maktabdagi ingliz tili o'qituvchim, Mrs. Johnson edi. Uning ta'limimga chuqur ta'siri bor edi va tillarga bo'lgan muhabbatimni chin dildan ilhomlantirdi.

Uni o'ziga xos qilgan narsa uning o'qitish uslubi edi. U shunchaki ma'ruza o'qimasdi – u darslarni interaktiv va qiziqarli qilardi. U mavzuni jonlantirish uchun o'yinlar, bahslar va real hayotiy misollardan foydalanardi. Uning fanga bo'lgan ishtiyoqi yuqumli edi.

Akademikadan tashqari, u juda qo'llab-quvvatlovchi edi. U har bir o'quvchining kuchli va zaif tomonlarini tushunishga vaqt ajratardi va bizni har doim o'z imkoniyatlarimizdan tashqariga chiqishga undardi. U menga o'zimga shubha qilganimda ham ishongan. Aytishlaricha, "Yaxshi o'qituvchi umidni ilhomlantirishi, tasavvurni uyg'otishi va o'rganishga muhabbatni singdirishi mumkin". U bularning barchasini men uchun albatta qildi.

questions.prompt: Do you live in a house or a flat?
questions.sampleA1:
I live in a house.

It is small.
questions.sampleA2:
I live in a flat.

It's small but nice.

I like it because it is near my work.
questions.sampleB1:
I live in a flat. It's not very big, but it's okay for me.

I think it's better than a house because it's easier to clean.

Also, it's in a good location near the shops.
questions.sampleB2: I live in a flat, actually — it's on the fourth floor of a fairly new block near the city centre. It's not huge, but it ticks all the boxes for me. The thing is, I prefer it to a house at the moment because there's hardly any upkeep, and everything I need is right on my doorstep.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Men kvartirada yashayman.

U kichkina, lekin yaxshi.

Menga u yoqadi, chunki u ishimga yaqin.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Men kvartirada yashayman. U juda katta emas, lekin men uchun yaxshi.

Menimcha, u uydan yaxshiroq, chunki uni tozalash osonroq.

Shuningdek, u do'konlarga yaqin yaxshi joyda joylashgan.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Men kvartirada yashayman, aslida. Bu shaharning chekkasida joylashgan nisbatan zamonaviy xonadon.

U juda katta bo'lmasa-da, unda menga kerak bo'lgan hamma narsa bor va ijara narxi juda maqbul.

Rostini aytsam, hayotimning shu bosqichida uni uyga nisbatan afzal ko'raman. Uni saqlash minimal va men jamoat transporti va mahalliy qulayliklarga yaqin bo'lish qulayligini qadrlayman.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - Do you live in a house or a flat?
idioms: home is where the heart is - "uy yurak bo'lgan joyda"
"A man's home is his castle" - "Odamning uyi uning qal'asidir"
sentenceStarters: "I currently live in..." - "Men hozirda ... da yashayman..."
"My accommodation is..." - "Mening turar joyim..."
"What I particularly like about where I live is..." - "Yashaydigan joyimda ayniqsa yoqtirgan narsa..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
I currently live in a flat, or apartment as some people call it. It's located on the fifth floor of a modern building in the city center.
The flat has two bedrooms, a living room, a small kitchen, and a bathroom. It's not particularly spacious, but it's perfectly adequate for my needs. What I especially appreciate is the location – I'm within walking distance of shops, restaurants, and public transportation.
Living in a flat has its advantages and disadvantages. On the positive side, there's less maintenance compared to a house, and I have access to amenities like a gym and parking. However, I sometimes miss having a garden or more private outdoor space. As the saying goes, "Home is where the heart is," and I've definitely made this flat feel like home.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men hozirda kvartirada yashayman, ba'zi odamlar uni apartament deb ham atashadi. U shahar markazidagi zamonaviy binoning beshinchi qavatida joylashgan.

Kvartirada ikkita yotoqxona, mehmonxona, kichik oshxona va hammom bor. U unchalik keng emas, lekin mening ehtiyojlarim uchun juda mos. Menga ayniqsa yoqadigan narsa - bu joylashuvi, men do'konlar, restoranlar va jamoat transportiga piyoda borishim mumkin.

Kvartirada yashashning afzalliklari va kamchiliklari bor. Ijobiy tomoni shundaki, uyga nisbatan kamroq ta'mirlash kerak va men sport zal va avtoturargoh kabi qulayliklardan foydalanishim mumkin. Biroq, men ba'zan bog' yoki ko'proq shaxsiy ochiq havoda bo'lishni sog'inaman. Aytishlaricha, "Uy - bu yurak qayerda bo'lsa, o'sha yer", va men bu kvartirani o'zimning uyimdek his qildim.

questions.prompt: What do you like to do on weekends?
questions.sampleA1: I like to play. I watch TV. I eat pizza.
questions.sampleA2: I like to play football on the weekend. And I like to watch TV, but sometimes I visit my grandma. She lives far away. I like to eat ice cream with her.
questions.sampleB1: On weekends, I like to relax and do fun things. For example, I often go to the cinema with my friends. I also like to play video games. Sometimes, I help my parents with chores around the house. I think it's important to have a good balance between fun and responsibility on the weekend.
questions.sampleB2: Well, weekends are when I finally get to unwind after a hectic week. I usually have a lie-in on Saturday, then meet up with friends for a coffee or a bite to eat. If the weather's nice, I'll head out for a walk. To be honest, I just try to make the most of my time off and recharge before Monday rolls around.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men o'ynashni yaxshi ko'raman. Men televizor ko'raman. Men pizza yeyman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men dam olish kunlarida futbol o'ynashni yaxshi ko'raman. Va televizor ko'rishni ham yaxshi ko'raman, lekin ba'zida buvimni ziyorat qilaman. U uzoqda yashaydi. U bilan muzqaymoq yeyishni yaxshi ko'raman.
questions.uzSampleB1: Dam olish kunlari men dam olishni va qiziqarli ishlar qilishni yoqtiraman. Masalan, men ko'pincha do'stlarim bilan kinoga boraman. Shuningdek, video o'yinlar o'ynashni ham yoqtiraman. Ba'zida ota-onamga uy ishlarida yordam beraman. Menimcha, dam olish kunlarida qiziqarli va mas'uliyat o'rtasida yaxshi muvozanat bo'lishi muhim.
questions.uzSampleB2: Dam olish kunlari hafta tartibidagi odatiy hayotdan xush kelibsiz tanaffusdir. Odatda, biroz dam olishga va kuchimni tiklashga harakat qilaman. Ochiq havoda vaqt o'tkazishni yoqtiraman, ehtimol piyoda sayr qilish yoki velosipedda sayr qilish. Shuningdek, do'stlarim bilan ovqatlanish yoki ichimliklar uchun uchrashishni yaxshi ko'raman. Bu muloqot qilish va dam olish uchun yaxshi imkoniyat. Ba'zan, kitob o'qish yoki musiqa asbobida chalish kabi sevimli mashg'ulotlarimga vaqt ajrataman. Umuman olganda, dam olish kunlarimdan unumli foydalanishga va o'zimga yoqadigan va qoniqarli bo'lgan ishlarni qilishga intilaman.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - What do you like to do on weekends?
idioms: all work and no play - "faqat ish va dam olish yo'q"
"Let your hair down" - "Dam olmoq, erkin bo'lmoq"
sentenceStarters: "On weekends, I typically enjoy..." - "Dam olish kunlari men odatda ... dan zavqlanaman..."
"My ideal weekend involves..." - "Mening ideal dam olish kunlarim ... ni o'z ichiga oladi..."
"I try to balance my weekends with..." - "Men dam olish kunlarimni ... bilan muvozanatlashga harakat qilaman..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Weekends are my time to unwind and enjoy activities that I don't have time for during the busy workweek.
On Saturday mornings, I typically sleep in a bit later than usual – it's a guilty pleasure of mine. Then I often meet friends for brunch or coffee. In the afternoon, I might go to the gym, explore the city, or catch up on some reading.
Sundays are usually more relaxed. I like to spend time with family, prepare meals for the upcoming week, and maybe watch a movie or series. I also try to do some light studying or work on personal projects.
I firmly believe that weekends should be a balance of relaxation and productive activities. As they say, "All work and no play makes Jack a dull boy," so I make sure to enjoy myself while also preparing for the week ahead.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Dam olish kunlari - bu men uchun dam olish va ish haftasida vaqt topolmaydigan mashg'ulotlardan zavqlanish vaqti.

Shanba kuni ertalab men odatdagidan biroz kechroq uxlayman - bu mening kichik bir zaifligim. Keyin ko'pincha do'stlarim bilan nonushta yoki qahva ichish uchun uchrashaman. Tushdan keyin sport zaliga borishim, shaharni o'rganishim yoki o'qishga vaqt ajratishim mumkin.

Yakshanba kunlari odatda yanada xotirjam o'tadi. Men oilam bilan vaqt o'tkazishni, kelgusi hafta uchun ovqat tayyorlashni va ehtimol kino yoki serial ko'rishni yaxshi ko'raman. Shuningdek, biroz yengil o'qish yoki shaxsiy loyihalar ustida ishlashga harakat qilaman.

Men dam olish kunlari dam olish va foydali mashg'ulotlarning muvozanati bo'lishi kerakligiga qat'iy ishonaman. Aytishlaricha, "Faqat ish va o'yin-kulgi bo'lmasa, odam zerikarli bo'lib qoladi", shuning uchun men o'zimdan zavqlanishga va shu bilan birga kelgusi haftaga tayyorgarlik ko'rishga harakat qilaman.

questions.prompt: What do you see in these pictures?
questions.sampleA1:
I see bus.

I see car.

People in bus.

Family in car.
questions.sampleA2:
In the picture, I see a bus and I see a car.

The bus has many people, and they are sitting and standing.

The car has a family, and they are happy.

I like the car because it is more comfortable.
questions.sampleB1:
Okay, in the first picture, I can see a bus with lots of people inside.

They are traveling somewhere, and some are standing.

In the second picture, there's a family in a car.

They look happy and are probably going on a trip.

I think both pictures show people traveling, but in different ways.
questions.sampleB2: In the first picture, I can make out the interior of what looks like a public bus. There are several passengers, some seated and one woman standing in the aisle with a backpack. It seems like a typical daily commute, with people going about their business. The second image, on the other hand, shows a family of four inside a car. The man is driving, and everyone, including the two children in the back with headphones, looks to be in good spirits. The main difference is the mode of transport: one is public and shared, while the other is a private family car, perhaps on a road trip or outing. Both depict travel, but with very different dynamics.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Men avtobusni ko'ryapman.

Men mashinani ko'ryapman.

Odamlar avtobusda.

Oila mashinada.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Rasmlarda men avtobusni va mashinani ko'ryapman.

Avtobusda ko'p odam bor, ular o'tiribdi va turibdi.

Mashinada bir oila bor va ular xursand.

Menga mashina yoqadi, chunki u qulayroq.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, birinchi rasmda men ichida ko'p odamlari bor avtobusni ko'ryapman.

Ular qayergadir sayohat qilishyapti, ba'zilari tik turishibdi.

Ikkinchi rasmda esa, mashinada bir oila bor.

Ular xursand ko'rinishadi va ehtimol sayohatga ketishyapti.

Menimcha, ikkala rasm ham odamlarning sayohat qilishini ko'rsatadi, lekin har xil usullarda.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Birinchi rasmda, men odamlar bilan to'lgan, jamoat avtobusining ichki qismini ko'rishim mumkin.

Bu odatdagi qatnovga o'xshaydi; ba'zi odamlar o'tiribdi, boshqalari esa turib, relslardan ushlab turishibdi.

Ikkinchi rasmda oila o'z mashinasida, go'yo sayohatda ekanligi ko'rsatilgan.

Ularning barchasi xursand va xotirjam ko'rinadi.

Ikkala rasm ham transportni tasvirlaydi, lekin biri jamoat transportini ta'kidlasa, ikkinchisi shaxsiy sayohatni namoyish etadi.

Avtobusning jamoaviy tajribasi va mashinaning shaxsiy muhiti o'rtasidagi farqni ko'rish qiziq.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - What do you see in these pictures?
sentenceStarters: "In the first picture, I can see..." - "Birinchi rasmda men ... ko'ryapman..."
"The second image shows..." - "Ikkinchi rasm ... ko'rsatmoqda..."
"These pictures contrast two different ways of..." - "Bu rasmlar ... ning ikki xil usulini taqqoslaydi..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
In these two pictures, I can see two different modes of transportation that people use in their daily lives.
The first image shows the interior of a public bus. We can see several passengers sitting and standing, holding onto the yellow handrails. There's a woman with a backpack in the foreground, and the bus appears to be fairly spacious with comfortable seating. The atmosphere seems calm, with passengers going about their daily commute. The natural lighting coming through the windows suggests it's daytime.
The second picture presents a completely different scene – a happy family traveling together in their private car. We can see what appears to be parents in the front seats and children in the back. The father is driving, and everyone seems to be in high spirits, smiling and enjoying the journey. The atmosphere is noticeably more intimate and personal.
These images effectively illustrate the contrast between public transportation and private vehicles. Each option has its own advantages and appeals to different people depending on their circumstances and preferences.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu ikki suratda odamlarning kundalik hayotda foydalanadigan ikki xil transport turini ko'rishim mumkin.

Birinchi suratda jamoat avtobusining ichki qismi tasvirlangan. Bir nechta yo'lovchilar o'tirgan va turgan, sariq tutqichlardan ushlab turganini ko'rishimiz mumkin. Old planda ryukzakli ayol bor va avtobus ancha keng va qulay o'rindiqli ko'rinadi. Atmosfera xotirjamdek, yo'lovchilar o'zlarining kundalik qatnovlari bilan band. Derazalardan tushayotgan tabiiy yorug'lik kunning kunduzi ekanligini ko'rsatadi.

Ikkinchi surat butunlay boshqa manzarani taqdim etadi – baxtli oila o'zining shaxsiy mashinasida birga sayohat qilmoqda. Old o'rindiqlarda ota-ona, orqa o'rindiqlarda esa bolalar ko'rinadi. Ota mashinani haydayapti va hamma xursand, tabassum qilib, sayohatdan zavqlanayotgandek. Atmosfera sezilarli darajada samimiy va shaxsiy.

Bu suratlar jamoat transporti va shaxsiy transport vositalari o'rtasidagi farqni samarali tarzda ko'rsatib beradi. Har bir variantning o'z afzalliklari bor va odamlarning vaziyatlari va xohishlariga qarab, ularga turli xil yoqadi.

questions.prompt: What are some of the advantages of driving a car?
questions.sampleA1:
I have a car.

I can go shop.

It is good.
questions.sampleA2:
I like driving a car.

It's good because I can go to many places.

And I can go to the supermarket with my car.

It's easy!
questions.sampleB1:
I think driving a car has some good advantages.

For example, you can go where you want, when you want.

It's more comfortable than the bus, in my opinion.

Also, you can carry a lot of things in the car, like shopping bags.

However, it can be expensive with the petrol.
questions.sampleB2: Well, the biggest advantage has to be the freedom it gives you. You can just hop in and go wherever you like, whenever you like, without being tied to a bus timetable. On top of that, it's really handy for lugging heavy shopping around. And to be honest, having your own private space to relax on a long journey is a huge plus.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Mening mashinam bor.

Men do'konga borishim mumkin.

Bu yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Menga mashina haydash yoqadi.

Bu yaxshi, chunki men ko'p joylarga borishim mumkin.

Va men mashinam bilan supermarketga borishim mumkin.

Bu oson!
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, mashina haydashning ba'zi yaxshi afzalliklari bor.

Masalan, qayerga xohlasangiz, qachon xohlasangiz, bora olasiz.

Mening fikrimcha, bu avtobusdan ko'ra qulayroq.

Shuningdek, mashinada ko'p narsalarni, masalan, xarid qilish paketlarini olib yurishingiz mumkin.

Biroq, benzin bilan qimmatga tushishi mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Mashina haydashning ba'zi afzalliklari, albatta, bor.

Eng aniq afzalligi - bu qulaylik va mustaqillikni ta'minlashidir. Siz jamoat transporti jadvaliga bog'liq emassiz, shuning uchun qayerga va qachon kerak bo'lsa, sayohat qilishingiz mumkin.

Yana bir afzalligi - katta yoki og'ir narsalarni osongina tashish imkoniyati, bu ayniqsa xarid qilish yoki narsalarni ko'chirish uchun foydalidir.

Bundan tashqari, mashina shaxsiy va qulay joyni ta'minlaydi, bu sizga dam olish va sayohatingizdan zavqlanish imkonini beradi.

Albatta, kamchiliklari ham bor, lekin mashina taqdim etadigan erkinlik katta plyusdir.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - What are some of the advantages of driving a car?
sentenceStarters: "One of the main advantages is..." - "Asosiy afzalliklardan biri..."
"From a practical standpoint, cars offer..." - "Amaliy nuqtai nazardan, mashinalar ... taklif qiladi..."
"I believe that having a car provides..." - "Menimcha, mashina egasi bo'lish ... beradi..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Driving a car offers several significant advantages that make it an attractive option for many people.
Firstly, and most importantly, cars provide unparalleled flexibility and freedom. You can travel wherever you want, whenever you want, without being restricted by bus schedules or train timetables. This is particularly valuable for those living in areas with limited public transportation options.
Secondly, cars offer privacy and comfort. You have your own personal space where you can listen to your favorite music, make phone calls, or simply enjoy the silence. For families, as shown in the picture, cars provide a bonding opportunity – road trips can create lasting memories.
Additionally, cars are extremely convenient for carrying heavy items, groceries, or luggage. Try doing your weekly shopping and bringing everything home on a bus!
Finally, in certain situations, driving can be faster than public transport, especially for door-to-door journeys. There's no waiting at bus stops or transferring between lines. As they say, "Time is money," and cars can save valuable time.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Avtomobil haydash ko'p odamlar uchun jozibador variantga aylantiradigan bir nechta muhim afzalliklarni taqdim etadi.

Birinchidan va eng muhimi, avtomobillar misli ko'rilmagan moslashuvchanlik va erkinlikni ta'minlaydi. Siz avtobus qatnovi yoki poyezd jadvali bilan cheklanmagan holda, xohlagan joyingizga, xohlagan vaqtingizda sayohat qilishingiz mumkin. Bu, ayniqsa, jamoat transporti imkoniyatlari cheklangan hududlarda yashovchilar uchun juda qimmatli.

Ikkinchidan, avtomobillar shaxsiy hayot va qulaylikni taklif etadi. Siz o'zingizning sevimli musiqangizni tinglashingiz, telefon qo'ng'iroqlarini amalga oshirishingiz yoki shunchaki sukutdan bahramand bo'lishingiz mumkin bo'lgan shaxsiy joyingizga ega bo'lasiz. Rasmda ko'rsatilganidek, oilalar uchun avtomobillar yaqinlashish imkoniyatini beradi – sayohatlar unutilmas xotiralarni yaratishi mumkin.

Bundan tashqari, avtomobillar og'ir narsalar, oziq-ovqat mahsulotlari yoki yuklarni tashish uchun juda qulay. Haftalik xaridlaringizni qilib, hamma narsani avtobusda uyga olib kelishga urinib ko'ring-chi!

Nihoyat, ba'zi hollarda, avtomobil haydash jamoat transportidan tezroq bo'lishi mumkin, ayniqsa, manzilgohdan manzilgohga sayohat qilish uchun. Avtobus bekatlarida kutish yoki liniyalar o'rtasida o'tish yo'q. Aytishlaricha, "Vaqt - pul", va avtomobillar qimmatli vaqtni tejashga yordam beradi.

questions.prompt: Why do some people prefer to use public transportation?
questions.sampleA1: I like bus. It is cheap. Car is expensive.
questions.sampleA2: I like the bus. It is easy. I don't have a car, and the bus is good for going to work. It's sometimes slow, but it's okay.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think some people like public transport because it's cheaper than having a car. Also, it can be less stressful because you don't have to drive in traffic. For example, you can read a book on the bus. However, it's not always very convenient.
questions.sampleB2: I suppose the main reason is cost — running a car is expensive once you factor in fuel, insurance and parking. Public transport works out far cheaper, especially for your daily commute. On top of that, it takes the stress out of driving in traffic. You can just sit back, read a book, and let someone else do the driving.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men avtobusni yaxshi ko'raman. U arzon. Mashina qimmat.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menga avtobus yoqadi. U oson. Mening mashinam yo'q, va avtobus ishga borish uchun yaxshi. Ba'zan sekin bo'ladi, lekin hechqisi yo'q.
questions.uzSampleB1: Xo'sh, menimcha, ba'zi odamlar jamoat transportini yaxshi ko'rishadi, chunki bu mashinaga ega bo'lishdan ko'ra arzonroq. Shuningdek, bu kamroq stressli bo'lishi mumkin, chunki siz tirbandlikda haydashingizga to'g'ri kelmaydi. Misol uchun, siz avtobusda kitob o'qishingiz mumkin. Biroq, bu har doim ham juda qulay emas.
questions.uzSampleB2: Ko'pchilik odamlar iqtisodiy va amaliy sabablarga ko'ra jamoat transportidan foydalanishni afzal ko'rishadi. Birinchi navbatda, avtomobilga egalik qilish va uni ta'mirlash xarajatlari, jumladan yoqilg'i, sug'urta va to'xtash joyi narxi juda yuqori bo'lishi mumkin. Jamoat transporti, ayniqsa, har kuni ishga borib kelish uchun ancha arzonroq variantni taklif etadi. Bundan tashqari, avtobus yoki poyezdlardan foydalanish tirband yo'llarda harakatlanish va to'xtash joylarini qidirish bilan bog'liq stressni kamaytirishi mumkin. Qatnovchilar bu vaqtdan dam olish yoki ishlash uchun foydalanishlari mumkin, bu odatda asabiylashtiradigan tajribani unumli tajribaga aylantiradi.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Why do some people prefer to use public transportation?
idioms: penny wise, pound foolish - "mayda narsalarda tejab, katta narsalarda yo'qotmoq"
sentenceStarters: "Many people choose public transport because..." - "Ko'p odamlar jamoat transportini tanlashadi, chunki..."
"From an environmental perspective..." - "Ekologik nuqtai nazardan..."
"I think the main reason is..." - "Menimcha, asosiy sabab..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
There are several compelling reasons why many people prefer public transportation over driving their own vehicles.
Firstly, cost is a major factor. Owning a car involves significant expenses – the purchase price, fuel, insurance, maintenance, and parking fees. Public transport is considerably more affordable, especially for daily commuters who can buy monthly passes.
Secondly, there are environmental benefits. Buses and trains can carry many passengers at once, reducing the number of vehicles on the road and lowering carbon emissions. Environmentally-conscious people often choose public transport to reduce their carbon footprint.
Additionally, public transportation eliminates the stress of driving in heavy traffic and finding parking. Commuters can use their travel time productively – reading, working, or simply relaxing. They don't have to worry about traffic jams or road rage.
Furthermore, in major cities with well-developed networks, public transport can actually be faster than driving, especially during rush hours. Dedicated bus lanes and metro systems bypass traffic entirely.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ko'pchilikning shaxsiy transport vositalarini haydashdan ko'ra jamoat transportidan foydalanishni afzal ko'rishining bir nechta asosli sabablari bor.

Birinchidan, xarajat asosiy omil hisoblanadi. Avtomobilga egalik qilish sezilarli xarajatlarni o'z ichiga oladi – sotib olish narxi, yoqilg'i, sug'urta, texnik xizmat ko'rsatish va to'xtash joyi uchun to'lovlar. Jamoat transporti ancha arzonroq, ayniqsa oylik chiptalar sotib oladigan har kuni qatnaydiganlar uchun.

Ikkinchidan, ekologik foydalari bor. Avtobuslar va poyezdlar bir vaqtning o'zida ko'plab yo'lovchilarni tashishi mumkin, bu yo'lda transport vositalari sonini kamaytiradi va karbonat angidrid chiqindilarini kamaytiradi. Atrof-muhitga befarq bo'lmagan odamlar ko'pincha karbon izlarini kamaytirish uchun jamoat transportini tanlashadi.

Bundan tashqari, jamoat transporti tirbandlikda haydash va to'xtash joyini topish stressini yo'q qiladi. Qatnovchilar o'zlarining sayohat vaqtlaridan unumli foydalanishlari mumkin – o'qish, ishlash yoki shunchaki dam olish. Ular tirbandlik yoki yo'ldagi jahldorlik haqida tashvishlanishlari shart emas.

Bundan tashqari, yaxshi rivojlangan tarmoqlarga ega yirik shaharlarda jamoat transporti aslida haydashdan tezroq bo'lishi mumkin, ayniqsa tirbandlik soatlarida. Maxsus avtobus yo'laklari va metro tizimlari tirbandlikni butunlay chetlab o'tadi.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a critical decision you have made.
questions.sampleA1: I choose pizza. It is my favourite. I like it.
questions.sampleA2: I decided to study English. It was difficult. But I want to travel. And I like English songs.
questions.sampleB1: A critical decision was when I decided to move to a new city. I was scared because I didn't know anyone. However, I thought it was important for my career. In my opinion, it was a good decision because I have more opportunities now. It was hard at first, but I am happy I did it.
questions.sampleB2: Right, so one of the most critical decisions I've ever made was turning down a well-paid job offer in another city to stay closer to my family. To be honest, it was a real tug-of-war in my head for weeks. On paper, the job was fantastic — great salary, brilliant career prospects, the whole package. But the thing is, it would have meant uprooting my entire life and seeing my parents maybe twice a year, and I just couldn't come to terms with that. I ended up sleeping on it for a good while, weighing up the pros and cons, and eventually I decided to follow my gut and stay put. Looking back, I honestly don't regret it for a second. As for how it's influenced my life, I'd say it shaped my priorities in a big way. It made me realise that money isn't everything — being near the people you love matters far more. Since then, I've built a career locally that I'm genuinely proud of, and I've been there for the big family moments I would otherwise have missed. When it comes to the factors that have the biggest impact on the decisions people make, I suppose it boils down to a few things. Money and job security are obviously huge for most people. But personal values and relationships play just as big a role, if not bigger. And I think fear of the unknown holds a lot of people back too. At the end of the day, the best decisions come from balancing your head with your heart.

Bu uzoq soatlar va moliyaviy noaniqlik bilan qiyin bo'ldi, lekin oxir-oqibat, noldan biror narsa qurish juda foydali bo'ldi. bulletPoints: Tell me about a critical decision you have made.
How has this decision influenced you and your life?
What factors have the highest impact on the decisions people make?
questions.sampleAnswer:
One of the most critical decisions I've made was choosing to pursue language studies rather than a career in engineering, which my family had expected.
This decision was incredibly difficult because it meant going against my parents' wishes. However, I knew deep down that my true passion lay in languages and communication. After much deliberation, I followed my heart and enrolled in a language program.
This decision has profoundly influenced my life. It led me to opportunities I never imagined – traveling, meeting people from different cultures, and finding a career that I genuinely love. Initially, my family was disappointed, but seeing my success and happiness, they've come to support my choice. It taught me that following your passion, while risky, can lead to genuine fulfillment.
As for factors that impact decisions, I believe several elements play crucial roles. Personal values and passions guide what feels right. Family expectations and societal pressure can influence us significantly. Practical considerations like finances and job security matter too. Ultimately, the best decisions come from balancing logic with intuition, as the proverb says, "Follow your heart, but take your brain with you."

Men qabul qilgan eng muhim qarorlardan biri bu oilam kutganidek, muhandislik sohasida emas, balki tilshunoslikni tanlash bo'ldi.

Bu qaror juda qiyin bo'ldi, chunki bu ota-onamning xohishlariga zid borishni anglatardi. Biroq, men yuragim tubida mening haqiqiy ishtiyoqim tillar va kommunikatsiyada ekanligini bilardim. Uzoq muhokamalardan so'ng, men yuragimga ergashdim va til dasturiga kirdim.

Bu qaror hayotimga juda katta ta'sir ko'rsatdi. Bu meni hech qachon tasavvur qilmagan imkoniyatlarga olib keldi - sayohat qilish, turli madaniyatlardan odamlar bilan uchrashish va chin dildan sevgan kasbimni topish. Dastlab, oilam xafa bo'ldi, lekin mening muvaffaqiyatim va baxtimni ko'rib, ular mening tanlovimni qo'llab-quvvatlay boshladilar. Bu menga ishtiyoqingizga ergashish, xavfli bo'lsa ham, chinakam qoniqishga olib kelishi mumkinligini o'rgatdi.

Qarorlarga ta'sir qiluvchi omillarga kelsak, menimcha, bir nechta element muhim rol o'ynaydi. Shaxsiy qadriyatlar va ishtiyoqlar nima to'g'ri ekanligini ko'rsatadi. Oila kutishlari va jamiyat bosimi bizga sezilarli ta'sir ko'rsatishi mumkin. Moliya va ish xavfsizligi kabi amaliy mulohazalar ham muhim. Oxir oqibat, eng yaxshi qarorlar mantiqni sezgi bilan muvozanatlashtirishdan kelib chiqadi, maqolda aytilganidek, "Yuragingga ergash, lekin miyangni ham olib yur".

questions.prompt: Homework Should Be Optional in Schools
questions.sampleA1: Homework... I don't like. School is... long. Homework is... too much.
questions.sampleA2: I think homework is okay, but sometimes it's too much. I have homework in math and English, and it takes a long time. I want to play with my friends, but I have to do homework. Maybe less homework is better.
questions.sampleB1: I think homework is important, but it shouldn't be too much. It helps me practice what I learn in class. However, sometimes I have so much homework that I don't have time for other things, like sports or hobbies. In my opinion, teachers should give us less homework, or at least make sure it's useful and not just busy work.
questions.sampleB2: Okay, so the idea that homework should be optional is a really interesting one, and I can genuinely see both sides of the argument. On the one hand, there's a strong case for making it optional. Let's face it, a lot of students these days are stretched pretty thin — they've got extracurricular activities, part-time jobs, and family responsibilities on top of school. Piling on endless homework can lead to stress and burnout, and honestly, some of it feels like busywork that doesn't add much value. Giving students the choice might actually encourage them to take ownership of their own learning. On the other hand, I do think homework serves an important purpose. It reinforces what you've covered in class and helps things sink in. It also builds discipline and good study habits, which come in handy later in life. If you made it completely optional, I suspect a fair few students would simply skip it altogether and fall behind. So where do I stand? Personally, I reckon the answer lies somewhere in the middle. Rather than scrapping homework entirely, schools should focus on quality over quantity. A couple of meaningful, well-thought-out tasks are worth far more than hours of mindless repetition. For instance, a short reading task or a couple of problems that genuinely make you think will stick with you far longer than twenty repetitive sums. That way, students still get the benefits without being run into the ground. At the end of the day, homework should support learning, not become a burden that puts kids off studying altogether.

Menimcha, o'qituvchilar bizga kamroq uyga vazifa berishlari kerak, yoki hech bo'lmaganda uning foydali ekanligiga ishonch hosil qilishlari kerak va shunchaki band bo'lish uchun emas.

Shuningdek, u o'qituvchilarga o'quvchilarning o'zlashtirish darajasini baholash va ular qiynalayotgan sohalarni aniqlash imkonini beradi.
Biroq, haddan tashqari ko'p uyga vazifa stress va charchoqqa olib kelishi mumkin, ayniqsa darsdan tashqari mashg'ulotlarda qatnashadigan yoki boshqa majburiyatlari bo'lgan o'quvchilar uchun.
Bundan tashqari, ixtiyoriy uyga vazifa o'quvchilarni o'z bilimlariga ko'proq egalik qilishga va ularni chinakam qiziqtirgan mavzularni o'rganishga undashi mumkin. Kompromiss sifatida uyga vazifalarni tanlash imkoniyatini taklif qilish yoki miqdor ustidan sifatga e'tibor qaratish mumkin, bu uyga vazifaning mazmunli va o'quv dasturiga mos bo'lishini ta'minlaydi.

questions.sampleAnswer:
The debate about whether homework should be optional in schools is a contentious issue in education. Let me present both perspectives.
Those who support making homework optional raise several valid points. Firstly, when students aren't burdened with mandatory assignments, they can focus on subjects they're genuinely passionate about, leading to deeper engagement and more meaningful learning. Secondly, excessive homework contributes to student stress and burnout, particularly when combined with extracurricular activities. Mental health experts have raised concerns about homework's impact on young people's well-being. Additionally, optional homework encourages self-directed learning, teaching students to take responsibility for their own education rather than just completing tasks because they're told to.
On the other hand, there are strong arguments for maintaining mandatory homework. It reinforces what's taught in class and provides essential practice – as the saying goes, "Practice makes perfect." Homework also helps teachers assess students' understanding and identify areas needing improvement. Furthermore, regular homework teaches crucial life skills like time management, self-discipline, and meeting deadlines – skills that are invaluable in the workplace.
In my view, a balanced approach works best – meaningful, reasonable amounts of homework that enhance learning without overwhelming students. Quality over quantity should be the guiding principle.

Maktablarda uy vazifasi majburiy bo'lishi kerakmi yoki yo'qmi degan bahs ta'lim sohasidagi bahsli masala hisoblanadi. Keling, ikkala nuqtai nazarni ham taqdim etay.

Uy vazifasini ixtiyoriy qilishni qo'llab-quvvatlovchilar bir nechta asosli fikrlarni ilgari suradilar. Birinchidan, o'quvchilar majburiy topshiriqlar bilan yuklanmaganida, ular chin dildan qiziqqan fanlarga e'tibor qaratishlari mumkin, bu esa chuqurroq ishtirok etishga va yanada mazmunli o'rganishga olib keladi. Ikkinchidan, haddan tashqari uy vazifasi, ayniqsa darsdan tashqari mashg'ulotlar bilan birgalikda, o'quvchilarning stressi va charchashiga sabab bo'ladi. Ruhiy salomatlik bo'yicha mutaxassislar uy vazifasining yoshlarning farovonligiga ta'siri haqida xavotir bildirishdi. Bundan tashqari, ixtiyoriy uy vazifasi o'z-o'zini boshqaruvchi o'rganishni rag'batlantiradi, o'quvchilarga shunchaki topshirilgani uchun vazifalarni bajarish o'rniga, o'z ta'limi uchun mas'uliyatni o'rgatadi.

Boshqa tomondan, majburiy uy vazifasini saqlab qolish uchun kuchli dalillar mavjud. Bu darsda o'tilgan narsalarni mustahkamlaydi va zarur amaliyotni ta'minlaydi - bekorga aytishmaydiki, "Mashq - mukammallik kaliti". Uy vazifasi, shuningdek, o'qituvchilarga o'quvchilarning tushunishini baholashga va yaxshilanishi kerak bo'lgan sohalarni aniqlashga yordam beradi. Bundan tashqari, muntazam uy vazifasi vaqtni boshqarish, o'z-o'zini intizomlash va belgilangan muddatlarga rioya qilish kabi muhim hayotiy ko'nikmalarni o'rgatadi - bu ko'nikmalar ish joyida juda qimmatlidir.

Mening fikrimcha, muvozanatli yondashuv eng yaxshi natija beradi - o'quvchilarni haddan tashqari yuklamasdan, o'rganishni yaxshilaydigan mazmunli, oqilona miqdordagi uy vazifasi. Sifat miqdoridan ustun bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan asosiy tamoyil bo'lishi lozim.
